summary: The cardholder starts a billing cycle with no balance, makes purchases that push the account above its $500 credit limit, and reaches statement close while still over limit. The scenario is designed to test that over-limit status exists at statement close and that a later minimum-payment obligation is represented but intentionally left unmet within this archetype.
assumptions: The account begins a new billing cycle with a $0.00 previous balance and an available credit limit of $500.00.
All purchase transactions are authorized and posted during the same billing cycle before the statement closes.
No payments, credits, interest charges, or other fees are posted before the statement close event, so the statement-closing balance equals the sum of purchases.

Although the contract also models a minimum payment obligation due after statement generation, this over-limit archetype focuses on the statement-close condition; the due date is placed after the end of the scenario and the obligation is therefore included only as an unmet due check reference.
A due_check event is used to reference the modeled minimum payment obligation even though no payment is made in this scenario.
